transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, thank you for having me, Doctor. I really appreciate your time. I, um... I guess I'm here because I've been having a hard time lately with... well, it sounds a little foolish for a man my age, to be honest, so I don't want to make too big a deal out of it. I hope it's okay to talk about this here. 

But I just can't seem to get past how rough and worn my face and hands have gotten. My wife, she tells me I'm being silly and that I just look like a man who's worked outdoors his whole life. And I know she's right, I do. But... I don't know, whenever I have to go into town, you know, to see the banker or talk to the county folks, I just feel like they're all staring right at me. Staring at the deep cracks, and the dark spots, and how my skin is sagging. I try not to let it bother me, but it just really gets to me. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it all right.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time thinking about these perceived flaws in your appearance, or do they interfere with your daily life in any way?

Well, um... I guess I do think about it a fair bit. Probably more than I should, I know. I don't mean to let it get in the way of things, but... well, sometimes it just does. 

Like, um, I've actually missed a couple of important video calls with the bankers lately. And I've put off some big decisions for the farm, just because... well, I couldn't get myself looking, you know, acceptable enough to sit down and face people. It sounds so silly when I say it out loud, I'm sorry. 

And my wife has been trying to get some new photos of me to help promote our little farm retreat and the crafts we sell, but I just... I've stopped agreeing to let her take them. I just can't stand the thought of people looking at those pictures and seeing how awful my skin looks. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about, Doctor? I hope I'm not making too big a fuss over nothing.
When you worry about how you look, is it mainly about your skin and the physical signs of aging, or are there other parts of your appearance that bother you as well?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. It's really just... just the skin, mostly. The deep lines and the dark spots on my hands and face. 

I mean, I know I'm an older fellow, and I'm not... I'm certainly not expecting to look like a young man anymore, I promise. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around obsessing over every little thing in the mirror, because I'm really not. It's just those specific areas that got so weathered and damaged from being out in the sun all these years. I guess I'm fairly content with the rest of me, all things considered. 

I hope that's... does that answer your question okay, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you describe how distressing these thoughts about your skin are for you when they come up?

Well, um... I really try not to let it get to me too much. I mean, it’s not like I’m... I’m not falling apart over it or anything, I promise. It just... it puts a bit of a pit in my stomach, I guess? 

When I start thinking about how weathered and, well, awful I look, it just makes me feel real low. I just kind of want to hide away for a bit so nobody has to look at me. But I know other folks have real, serious problems, much worse things to worry about than an old farmer's skin, so I try to just push it out of my mind and get back to work as best I can. I really don't want to sound like a complainer, you know? 

Is that... does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm not making it sound like a bigger deal than it really is.
When you think about your skin looking worn or damaged, are you mainly worried about how it looks to others, or are you more concerned that it might mean something serious is wrong with your health?

Well, um... I suppose it's mostly about how it looks to other folks. I'm not really worried about my health, I mean, I feel fine physically. It's just... 

Well, what really brought me in here is that I just can't seem to get past how rough and worn my face and hands look. I know I shouldn't care so much, but whenever I have to deal with the bankers or the county folks, I just feel like they're staring right at all the cracks and the dark spots and the sagging skin. 

My wife, bless her, she always tells me I just look like a man who's worked outdoors his whole life, and I know she means well. I really try to believe her, I do. But I just can't shake the feeling that everyone else is judging me for looking so... so damaged. 

I know it's probably silly to care what a banker thinks of my face, and I'm sorry if I'm wasting your time with this. Am I making sense, Doctor? I hope I'm answering your question the right way.

When you look at your skin, do you feel that the lines, spots, or sagging look abnormal or different from how they actually are, or do you feel they look about how you would expect for someone your age and lifestyle?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I know my wife says I just look like a guy who's worked in the sun, and I'm sure she's right. I really don't want to sound like I'm completely out of touch with reality or anything. 

But when I look in the mirror, it just... it feels like it's so much worse than it should be. Like, I see other fellas my age around town, other guys who have farmed their whole lives, and their skin just doesn't look as... as ruined as mine does. It feels like the spots are darker and the lines are deeper than they ought to be, even for someone who's been outside as much as I have. 

But maybe I'm just being too hard on myself? I really try not to blow things out of proportion, I promise. I know it's just skin. Does that... does that sound like a normal way to feel, Doctor? I hope I'm not sounding crazy saying that.

When you look at your skin and feel upset, are you mainly focused on specific features—like the exact depth of the lines or the darkness of the spots—or is it more of a general feeling that something is wrong with how you look overall?

Well, um... I guess it's a bit of both, but... I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm obsessing over every little detail, because I'm not. I try to just take things as they come. But... 

I suppose I do get pretty caught up on the specific things. Like I said before, it's just... I can't seem to get past how rough my face and hands look. When I'm talking to the bankers or the county folks, I just feel like they're staring right at those specific cracks, and the dark spots, and the way the skin sags. It's not just a general feeling, it's... it's those exact things that I just can't stop focusing on. 

Even though my wife, like I mentioned, she always tells me I just look like a man who's worked outdoors his whole life. I really try to listen to her, and I know I shouldn't be so fixated on a few spots and lines. I'm sorry to keep bringing it up, I just... I want to make sure I'm answering you right. Is it... is it okay that I focus on those specific parts, Doctor? I hope I'm not making too much of a fuss over it.
